name: The Conversion of Saint Paul
history: Saul of Tarsus, a zealous Pharisee, was travelling to Damascus to arrest followers of Jesus when a light from heaven threw him to the ground and the risen Christ asked him, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?’ Blinded, then healed and baptised, the persecutor became the Apostle of the Gentiles. The feast closes the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity.
life: Saul was a Jew of the dispersion, born at Tarsus in Cilicia, a Roman citizen and a student of the great rabbi Gamaliel in Jerusalem. He approved the stoning of Stephen and set out to destroy the Church. Acts tells his conversion three times. On the road he heard Christ name Himself as one with those he was hunting: ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.’ Led blind into Damascus, he fasted for three days until a disciple named Ananias, sent by the Lord, laid hands on him, and something like scales fell from his eyes. He was baptised and began at once to preach the Christ he had opposed. Paul never forgot it. He called himself the least of the apostles, unfit to be called one, because he had persecuted the Church of God, and he spent the rest of his life carrying the Gospel to the nations, until he was beheaded at Rome.
prayerTo: Saint Paul, you were struck down on the road and raised up by grace. Pray for all who oppose the faith, that the light of Christ may meet them as it met you. Pray for the unity of Christians, and for me, that the scales may fall from my eyes and I may live no longer for myself but for Christ who lives in me. Amen.
penance: Ananias was afraid to go to Saul, but he went. Reach out today to someone you find difficult, and pray for Christians of other traditions near you.
meditation: ‘Who are you, Lord?’ was Paul’s first prayer as a Christian. Ask it today, and let Christ answer.
prayer: O God, Who taught the whole world by the preaching of Your blessed Apostle Paul, grant, we beseech You, that we who today celebrate his conversion may draw nearer to You by way of example. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
